page.layout: One block of text, one printed page on the scan: a heading at full width at the top (title in capitals and spaced type, with the subtitle below), then one column of running text from top to bottom with marginal-free layout. No margin notes, no running head, no page number other than the printed "2" at the top left corner.

main_text.l: est praenuntiata, ac praedicta ab ipsis
Non auferetur sceptrum de Iuda, nec Dux de femore eius,
donec veniat qui mittendus est: & ipse erit expectatio Gentium.
Ecce Virgo concipiet, & pariet filium, & vocabitur nomen
eius Emanuel: quod est interpretatum, nobiscum Deus. Isa. cap.7.
Paruulus natus est nobis, & filius datus est nobis. Isa.9.cap.

l.i: Exulta, & lauda habitatio Sion: quia magnus in medio
Et tu Beth-leem terra Iuda, nequaquam minima es in prin-
cipibus Iuda: ex te enim exiet Dux, qui regat populum meum
Sic Deus dilexit mundum ut filium suum unigenitum
daret: ut omnis qui credit in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam
Lauda, & laetare filia Sion: quia ecce ego venio, & habitabo
in medio tui, ait Dominus. Zachariae cap.2.

page.notes: The scan shows show-through from the reverse page (faint mirrored text, e.g. "ANNO D. GVILIELMI ROVILLIVM" and a faint line near the head), which was omitted. The printed page has no running head, catchword or signature. Initial "N" of "Non" and "E" of "Ecce" are decorated/large initials, transcribed as ordinary letters. The "V" in "Virgo" and "Vocabitur" and "Vitam" are printed with a long-tailed form; read as V/U per the spelling rule. Some verse-reference digits are small and slightly blurred (e.g. "4 9", "cap.7.", "cap.s.") and are given as best read.
